BOOP! joyfully celebrates the timeless appeal of Betty Boop while bringing her into the 21st century with high-energy Broadway flair.

With a zippy score, terrific tap numbers choreographed by director Jerry Mitchell, energetic performances from a top-notch cast, and a plot that doesn’t tax your brain, Boop! is one of the feel-good musicals of the year.
You will likely have more fun at Boop! than in many other theaters this spring; this is an old-fashioned stage-frolic filled show, with big songs and bigger dancing.
Hurtling towards us through metaphysical universes and a sometimes bumpy production, Rogers arrives fully-formed: a star.

Even so, the entire evening is lots of fun.
It seems that Boop! The Musical has a new star rather than an old one.

Still, for the most part, “Boop!” too rarely rises above the level of pleasant fluff during its two-and-half-hours, which can be frustrating since the show’s potential for greatness is obviously within reach.
Little of it feels original, and none of it feels necessary.

Yet all this effort is in service of one of the most maladroit storylines Broadway has encountered in years, with cardboard characters that serve plot purposes only, a book that doesn’t listen to the lyrics and dialogue that doesn’t listen to itself.
Betty Boop may be ready for her close-up, but this isn’t the vehicle she deserves.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this nostalgic musical, with most praising breakout star Jasmine Amy Rogers' sensational debut and Jerry Mitchell's dazzling choreography, while questioning the show's thin story and unclear purpose.

vs.sum: One of Broadway's least comfortable theaters, with notoriously tight legroom and narrow seats. The lack of rake means tall patrons in front block your view. Restrooms are in the basement, creating long intermission lines. For legroom, target Row A or N in Orchestra.

acc.note: 6 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No steps from sidewalk. Infrared devices available.

vr.q: This was the most insane thing I've ever experienced... it made what is objectively a very silly evening also feel really special and meaningful.
If you are coming to New York and you're visiting and you are just looking for a silly fun time and you are okay with the writing not being the greatest, Boop is a silly fun time.
I think the show is worth seeing if only for the brilliant performance of Jasmine Amy Rogers. The energy is infectious. It's a very joyful show.
International icon and cartoon character Betty Boop now has her own Broadway show, and it was a bit of a mixed bag for me.
Structurally, for me, it didn't hold up together for what I was trying to achieve... but people around me seem to have a great time, so I suggest you go and check it out for yourself.

I think the whole thing is a little fundamentally and inherently misguided. But it's great to look at. She's sensational. There's some brilliant production numbers. It's easy to listen to. It is satisfying and entertaining in the most basic sense, but I just think we need a better story.
